prior.sentence: It typically consists of a handle attached to a rigid shaft, with a shaped tip at the shaft’s working end.
Handles may be molded from plastic, wood, or rubberized materials to provide a comfortable grip and resist slipping.
The working tip may be flat, cross-shaped, hexagonal, or star-shaped to fit different fastener recesses.
Some models have magnetic tips that help hold small metal fasteners in place during positioning.
A user seats its tip in a fastener head and twists the handle to rotate the fastener.
Applying steady pressure while turning helps keep the tip engaged and reduces the chance of it slipping out.
Reversing the direction of rotation can loosen a tightened fastener or back it out of its hole.
On models with replaceable bits, a user can swap the working tip to fit another head pattern.
During household furniture assembly, it is often used to secure joints with threaded fasteners.
At an electronics repair bench, small versions are useful when working with tiny fasteners inside devices.
In vehicle maintenance, it may be used to remove or secure fasteners on interior panels and trim.
On a construction site, workers may keep one in a tool pouch for fastening tasks away from a workbench.
It enables people to join or separate parts by tightening or removing the fasteners that hold them together.
It can tighten small terminal fasteners in electrical equipment, helping secure wires when the circuit is safely de-energized.
Its handle provides leverage for applying controlled rotational force to threaded fasteners that may be difficult to turn by hand.
It is used to tighten or loosen tiny fasteners in eyeglass frames, helping secure temples and hinges during repairs.
Many shafts are made from hardened steel to withstand repeated twisting against resistant fasteners.
Some shafts have a hexagonal section near the handle that accepts a wrench for additional turning force.
A ratcheting handle turns the shaft in repeated short strokes while the tip stays seated in the fastener head.
A torque-limiting model stops transmitting turning force when it reaches its preset threshold.
Aboard a small boat, one may be kept handy for fastening access-hatch hardware during maintenance.
In a model-making studio, a small version can secure miniature components during assembly.
It can turn the worm-drive mechanism on a band clamp to tighten the band around a hose.
